findings.title: Use the existing exact-envelope budget predicate when packing product review batches
findings.classification_detail: Source-confirmed engineering opportunity: the batch packer checks only the structured envelope, whereas the final server checks the doubled, escaped wire result as well. A complete public escaping-heavy fixture was not executed, so its exact failure threshold and frequency remain unmeasured.

source_references.evidence: The batch owns one scoped read audit and halves the first portion or stops a nonempty batch, but fits at 2521-2524 checks only JSON bytes of the structured envelope against 24 KiB.
The existing shared predicate checks both the structured payload at 24 KiB and the exact text-plus-structured MCP result at 64 KiB.
The handler runs the scenario before final successResult; a final budget miss converts the entire successful read payload to RESULT_LIMIT.
The public tool promises up to 20 exact frozen blocks within the response budget and exposes the batch implementation.
Legacy review text is returned unchanged in portions; complete portions receive their receipt, and incomplete portions retain exact-prefix continuations.
The published batch allows up to 20 items and legacy portions permit arbitrary string text up to 4096 characters. It does not exclude quotation/backslash-heavy text.
An existing unexecuted regression assertion explicitly distinguishes a payload fitting 24 KiB from its escaped full result exceeding 64 KiB.
Existing public Unicode coverage checks both budgets, but the direct batch Unicode test asserts the structured envelope only. Unicode byte expansion does not cover nested JSON escaping.
The specification review reader already adapts portion size with boundedSuccessResult and preserves old cursor identities.
The exact product-source batch already budgets both envelope copies before accepting a candidate item. This recommendation is not to add another batching API.

current_execution_path: tools/call -> productTool input validation -> readProductReviewBatch -> request-local source verification -> structured-only fits -> output schema validation -> server.successResult -> boundedSuccessResult.

If the packer accepts a structured envelope whose escaped wire result is too large, the final server discards the whole batch response and returns a bounded RESULT_LIMIT. The read audit and packing work have already occurred.
existing_optimizations: Existing bounded 1-20 item API, request-local immutable integrity reuse, pending-only filtering, adaptive first-item portion size, partial-item continuation and final whole-result rejection.
A shared exact-wire predicate already exists; specification review reads use it, and product source batches independently implement both limits.
No oversized successful result is silently truncated or sent. This is avoidable read/retry work, not an unbounded-response vulnerability.
findings.unnecessary_work_or_restriction: An escaping-heavy but otherwise valid review batch can pass the local packer and then lose every useful item at the server boundary, requiring the actor to infer a smaller limit and repeat source verification and reading. The packer has the full envelope needed to avoid that retry.

reproducible_scenario.setup: Use the existing isolated PRD review fixture with several complete short semantic blocks containing dense quotation marks or safe non-path escape characters. Keep each block below the 4096-character portion limit. Leave verdicts pending and use the legacy representation first.
steps: Vary several block lengths in the approximately 1800-3500 character range until readProductReviewBatch accepts an envelope below 24 KiB whose exact content-plus-structured serialization exceeds 64 KiB; calculate both byte counts, not character estimates.

Call the public product_review_get_batch with the same context, start_index and limit. The final server predicate should reject that whole candidate today even though the direct batch packer accepted it.
Compare with a smaller limit and with the revised predicate; collect all continuations, reconstruct every exact block and compare final receipts.
reproducible_scenario.assumptions: The exact boundary depends on context and metadata sizes; the numerical source-length range is fixture guidance, not a measured result. No live customer data or managed YAML parsing is needed.

findings.minimal_sufficient_recommendation: Replace the structured-only fits predicate in readProductReviewBatchSources with a Boolean check of the existing boundedSuccessResult on the exact candidate envelope. Retain the current halve-first-portion and stop-after-fitted-items behavior. Do not increase limits, truncate source material, introduce a new API or globally cache source reads.
findings.expected_qualitative_effect: Escaping-heavy batches should return the largest currently packable useful prefix instead of failing after reading it. This removes avoidable full-batch retries and aligns local packing with the final boundary. Ordinary batches should preserve their present behavior.

confidence.end_to_end_fixture_failure: medium until the proposed fixture runs

guarantees.correctness: Preserve exact frozen text, item order, pending filtering, source verification and complete-read receipts. Do not issue a receipt for an incomplete portion.
guarantees.compatibility: No input/output schema or budget change. Page boundaries may shrink, but public callers already must follow per-item and next-item continuations; retain cursor and receipt identities independent of page size.
guarantees.state_isolation: The tool stays read-only and request-scoped. No mutable source cache moves to module scope.
guarantees.recovery: Retain the current explicit RESULT_LIMIT when even one minimal portion cannot fit; otherwise preserve a resumable fitted prefix.
guarantees.security: Keep both exact response caps, non-reflecting errors and immutable source integrity checks. Never solve the issue by disabling the final guard.

measurement_plan: Use synthetic ASCII, multibyte Unicode, quotation-heavy and escape-heavy block sets with identical exact source content before and after the change.

Record structured bytes, exact full-result bytes, returned item/portion counts, RESULT_LIMIT responses, retries, source-validation events and end-to-end read-call count. Report server time separately from actor/model time.

Compare reconstruction and final receipt equality for every item and verify each response advances or returns the established explicit single-item limit error. No savings percentage is claimed by this audit.
validation_plan: Add a public stdio regression for a candidate that fits the structured limit but not the doubled escaped wire limit.

Reuse product review efficiency/recovery tests for pending scans, partial continuations, stale context, final consistency and unchanged receipts; inspect side effects and authorize execution separately.
Keep the existing exact-envelope unit tests and product source batch envelope tests as boundary references.
findings.rough_complexity: Small implementation change at one local predicate; small-to-medium regression-fixture work to hit both boundaries deterministically.

findings.title: Bind lazy packaged-schema compilation to the runtime's captured startup contract
findings.classification_detail: Source-confirmed lifecycle mismatch: runtime identity is frozen at startup, while some packaged schemas are first read lazily from mutable disk later. The disk-replacement scenario is inferred from these paths and existing replacement-test semantics; it was not executed during this audit.

source_references.evidence: The runtime digests executable/JSON artifacts, verifies the stamp once and deliberately captures identity before serving so later disk replacements cannot relabel loaded code.
workflow_runtime_info returns that captured identity and implemented registry capabilities.
The per-kind validator map is empty initially; the first validation awaits a filesystem schema read and compiles it, then retains the validator.
The product record schema is also read only when compileSchema first runs. A promise deduplicates this work thereafter, but does not tie the first read to startup bytes.
Tool input validators and published schemas are constructed eagerly from the package schema, while output validation calls the independently lazy validateProductRecord after running the scenario.
The stamp records runtime artifact digests; it does not provide the later lazy loader with the original schema bytes.
Package generation replaces schema files and exports tool contracts from the built registry. This is source inspection only; the script was not run.

Tests explicitly require process A to keep A's identity when files are replaced by same-version B. They also test missing/mixed startup metadata and changed-schema identity after a newly started process. The inspected tests do not exercise A's first lazy schema read after replacement.
Another eager schema/Ajv instance validates semantic input; domain checks must remain separate from any shared immutable-schema ownership.
Technical Design has another eager schema validator with additional sensitivity/title/applicability checks.
Roadmap has another eager validator and domain-specific checks. Existing schema parsing is duplicated; no startup-cost measurement was performed.

current_execution_path: Process A imports its tool registry and identity module. Tool inputs/public schemas are captured eagerly; runtimeIdentity records startup artifact digests and is frozen.
Without a prior call requiring a particular state/product record validator, its compiled-schema slot remains empty.

If packaged schema files are replaced before that first call, state.validate or product.compileSchema reads the replacement bytes. A can then validate using B's contract while still publishing/returning A's captured identity and eager input definitions.
existing_optimizations: Identity is intentionally captured once, has an embedded-stamp consistency check, rejects mixed/missing startup artifacts, avoids exposing local paths and has explicit refresh/restart guidance.
Product record compilation already shares one promise and validates the packaged schema before use; state schemas already retain compiled validators by artifact kind.
Eager product input validators are reused across requests and consume errors synchronously. This is not a recommendation to share request contexts, stores or source-verification results.
The observed live/local stamp difference alone does not demonstrate this scenario; immutable installation paths and prompt restarts can prevent it operationally.
findings.unnecessary_work_or_restriction: A same-path package replacement can create an internally mixed validation contract after a verified startup. Valid calls may fail against a schema different from the advertised one, causing unnecessary diagnostics, reopen/retry cycles and potentially post-scenario output rejection. Existing identity evidence cannot explain that behavior accurately because it remains the earlier identity.

reproducible_scenario.setup: Extend the existing copied-package runtime-identity fixture, never the installed package or live store. Start A and request only workflow_runtime_info so product/state lazy validators remain cold.
steps: Replace only the fixture's packaged product schema with a valid B variant that changes validation of a selected success definition, or replace an unused state-kind schema with an incompatible valid B variant. Keep A running.

Issue the first read-only product scenario that triggers product output validation, or exercise a selected state validator in the isolated fixture, using an input still matching A's eagerly advertised contract.

Observe A's response and runtime identity, then start a new coherent B process. Today A's lazy validation path reads B from disk even though its identity remains A; the proposed lifecycle should make A use the captured A contract or report a precise unavailable/mismatched contract before scenario work.
reproducible_scenario.assumptions: The scenario requires in-place package-file replacement while A remains alive and at least one cold lazy validator. It is not asserted for immutable-version installation directories, already-warmed validators, or the currently serving process.

findings.minimal_sufficient_recommendation: Capture immutable packaged schema bytes once at serving initialization and verify that snapshot against the artifacts used for the captured runtime identity. Keep lazy compilation, but compile from that snapshot rather than rereading disk. Reuse the existing product schema owner where practical, without merging domain-specific checks. A changed/missing snapshot must yield an explicit identity/contract-unavailable path before a scenario is executed. Do not rehash all files on every request or introduce a global cache of workflow data.
findings.expected_qualitative_effect: Keep identity, advertised schemas and actual validation coherent throughout one serving lifetime. Avoid mixed-contract failures and repeated investigative reads after package replacement. Central immutable ownership can also remove duplicate package-schema reads/parses, but startup and memory benefits are unmeasured and secondary to contract coherence.

guarantees.correctness: Preserve schema self-validation, supported-definition checks, Unicode checks, sensitivity checks and all domain-level rules. A new package takes effect only in a new coherent serving lifecycle.
guarantees.compatibility: Preserve existing tool names, envelope versions and digest semantics. Do not silently change an already serving process's identity to match replacement files.
guarantees.state_isolation: The retained data is immutable package contract data only, bounded by the fixed packaged schema set and serving/process lifetime. Request contexts, validator diagnostics, mutable workflow state and integrity audits remain request-local; consume mutable Ajv error arrays synchronously.
guarantees.recovery: Continue explicit refresh/restart guidance. Add a deterministic mismatched-snapshot diagnostic instead of allowing cold validation to adopt replacement files silently.
guarantees.security: Snapshot validation must use the already verified artifact digest domain, reject mixed/nonregular artifacts and keep paths/source values out of public errors. Do not weaken filesystem or ledger validation.

measurement_plan: Compare cold initialization and first-call latency separately for runtime_info, one state-kind validation and one product read in isolated same-version fixtures.
Count packaged-schema reads/parses/compilations and record initialization memory as well as post-first-call memory, before considering any further consolidation.
Measure the A/B replacement case by identity, published contract and actual validator behavior, not timing alone. Repeat with warm validators and immutable installation paths as controls.
validation_plan: Add a cold-validator A/B replacement regression beside runtime-identity.test.mjs, covering product output and at least one lazy state schema.
Assert A retains A semantics and identity after replacement, a coherent restarted B uses B, and inconsistent startup/snapshot evidence stays unavailable.

Verify unchanged contract publication, domain validation, concurrent error isolation, and no writes to real homes/stores. Existing identity, metadata and diagnostics tests are source evidence only until separately authorized execution.
findings.rough_complexity: Medium: align ownership across runtime identity and two schema loaders, preserve lazy compilation, and add isolated replacement regressions. Sharing additional eager domain validators is optional and should not expand the minimal fix.
